segments.text: An urban legend with an eerie similarity to the serial killings from 18 years ago. It's said that Emio would appear before crying girls and offer them "a smile that will last forever". His murder victims would later be found with a smiley-faced paper bag over their heads.
From Nintendo
The urban legend was actually reality, as these murders were indeed committed by a serial killer named Minoru Tsuzuki.

A police inspector overseeing Junko and Daisuke's investigation efforts. He and Shunsuke Utsugi previously worked together on the unsolved murders from 18 years ago, and requests the help of the Utsugi Detective Agency.
From Nintendo
A police detective working on the Eisuke Sasaki case. She's considered something of a workaholic by her peers and is notoriously strict on herself and her fellow detectives.
From Nintendo

Her parents died when she was a young child, so she spent some of her childhood raised by her grandparents alongside her older brother Makoto. On Junko's ninth birthday, while their grandparents were out looking for a gift for Junko, Makoto picked eggplant flowers from the garden to give to her, not knowing that Junko was growing them herself to give to Makoto on his birthday. Junko was angered by this; she yelled that she hated her brother for ruining the surprise she had prepared for him. She fled the house, leaving Makoto alone.

At some point, Junko started crying outside, leading to her being threatened by serial killer Minoru Tsuzuki. Makoto eventually found her and came to her defense; Tsuzuki ultimately abandoned trying to kill Junko and instead kidnapped Makoto, driving off with him. Junko was unable to catch them and eventually returned home in tears alone after 9:00pm. Junko did not speak to anyone about Makoto, and was traumatised by the incident. A search party was formed to look for Makoto, but he was never found.

In adulthood, Junko became a detective under Kimiharu Kamada to find Makoto, gaining a reputation among the police force as being very strict and a hard worker. One night, she discovered the unmoving Eisuke Sasaki lying down; she gave him chest compressions in an attempt to revive him, but soon discovered that he had died by suicide. She decided to place a paper bag with a smiley-face drawn on it onto Sasaki's head, so that his death would be connected to the "Serial Girl Murders" committed by Tsuzuki and give her reason to re-investigate her brother's disappearance.

Junko was assigned to the investigation of Sasaki's death, partnered with Daisuke Kamihara. She maintained strict supervision over the investigation, to the point of refusing to allow the protagonist and Shunsuke Utsugi to view the body after they were called to the scene by Kamada. Sasaki's death was soon considered to be a homicide and was connected to the "Serial Girl Murders", as she had hoped.

One night, Junko was stalked to her apartment by a man in a smiley-face paper bag, who she assumed was Tsuzuki, though it was actually Makoto. Eventually, Junko forced the protagonist off the investigation and soon after found her unmasked brother who, though still alive, was amnesiac. As he started to remember who he was, Tzuzuki appeared and attacked them; Makoto killed him with a gun in self-defense. Junko then instructed Makoto to hide as the protagonist arrived to the scene, with Junko picking up the gun to make it look like she was the one who shot Tsuzuki. She threatened the protagonist with the gun until Makoto emerged attempting to kill him for making Junko cry. However, he was thwarted by the arrival of Kamihara.
In the aftermath, Junko resigned as a detective, married Kamihara, helped with Makoto's recovery, and sent the protagonist a letter of apology.
A young police detective working alongside Junko Kuze on her investigation. He's often scolded by Junko for his carefree attitude and approach to detective work.
From Nintendo

A police officer the protagonist comes across. She is transferred to a different police station between the events of Famicom Detective Club: The Girl Who Stands Behind and Emio - The Smiling Man: Famicom Detective Club.

A cheerful and patient assistant detective from the Utsugi Detective Agency who possesses a keen intuition. He is assigned to investigate the circumstances of Eisuke Sasaki's death at the request of the police.
From Nintendo
A hard-working assistant detective working alongside the protagonist. Despite her kind-hearted nature, Ayumi is often praised for her interrogation skills.
From Nintendo
Junko Kuze's older brother. He dissapeared 18 years ago and hasn't been seen since.
From in-game description
A man who was a key person in the serial murders of girls 18 years ago, but went missing and was never found.

In childhood, he and his younger sister Emiko lived in Irumo Village and were subjected to constant abuse from their father. Minoru had the idea of wearing a paper bag with a crudely-drawn smile on it, which managed to help cheer Emiko up, and the two would thereafter play together while wearing such paper bags. When Emiko was found dead one day from drowning after they planned on running away from their father together, Minoru considered his father responsible for the death and murdered him in retaliation. Minoru attended Emiko's funeral, and placed her paper bag in her coffin. Minoru was later sentenced to juvenile detention for the murder.

While serving his sentence, Minoru was observed by the detention center director as being very quiet and honest, while also often muttering to himself. He took an interest in cars and was encouraged to pursue a career in automotive repair; he took this to heart and studied to become a mechanic, easily passing his certification examination. After this, Minoru told the director that he planned on getting a car and driving his sister around in it. Knowing that Emiko was his only sister, the director found this odd and would later speculate that Minoru was trying to pretend that Emiko's death never happened.

Upon his release, Minoru returned to Irumo Village. He was welcomed fondly and started helping with farm work, though the villagers noted the same behaviours the director did. Minoru later left the village.

Minoru ended up in Kamematsu City, where he discovered and was drawn to Todoroki Motors. He worked there for a time, with the owner and his wife taking him in and treating him as a surrogate son. He eventually left and was gifted a car, then went on to live in a nearby apartment.

Following this, his mental state began to deteriorate; he came to believe that every crying teenage girl was Emiko, and as such, would approach them with a paper bag with a smiley-face on it; if they stopped crying, he would leave them alone, otherwise, he would kill them by strangulation and leave another such bag on their corpse so that they would have "a smile that lasts forever", thus instigating the urban legend of Emio, the Smiling Man. He additionally cut his own face open, leaving a lot of blood in his apartment, so that he himself would have a permanent smile. He soon became a suspect in the girls' murders, but managed to evade the police.

One of his attempted victims was Junko Kuze, though his attempt at killing her was thwarted by her brother Makoto. Minoru decided to abandon killing Junko and instead kidnapped Makoto. Makoto was rendered amnesiac from the ordeal; Minoru took advantage of this to prevent him from finding out who he was. It was not until eighteen years later that Minoru was brought to justice; in another attempt to kill Junko, who had since become a detective to find Makoto, Makoto arrived and, regaining some memories, killed Minoru in self-defense.
A third-year student at Minami Daisan Junior High. She has been friends with Eisuke Sasaki since childhood.
